_comment: THE NIGHT, as one GO button. Rebuilt 2026-08-08 from the shape the QLC+
show ran: Warm Up -> Idle -> Deep -> Spiral -> Cathedral -> Peak -> Build
-> Drop -> Landing. Those were six Collections in the workspace and the
porter skipped every one of them ('Collection -- rebuild with motion
primitives'), so the cue list has been missing since the port. This is it.
A cue is the same three slots a preset is, plus a fade and an optional
hold. 'fade' and 'hold' are in BEATS, not seconds -- everything authored in
this engine is musical, and a cue list that ignored tempo would be the one
surface drifting out of the music it is cueing.
Every 'hold' here is 0, which means every cue waits for GO. That is
deliberate and it is why the original worked: the operator decides when the
drop is. Set a hold on a cue only if you genuinely want it to leave on its
'macro' restores a shape where the cue wants a particular one. Cues that
omit it leave whatever is dialled in alone, so the list does not fight an
name: Night

cues.name: Warm Up
cues.notes: Doors. Everything on the ball, small and warm, nothing moving fast enough to look at.

cues.name: Idle
cues.notes: Room filling. The wave opens up and the heads stop moving together.

cues.name: Deep
cues.notes: Colour arrives. Spread to a half cycle so the sweep reads as a chase rather than a bar.

cues.name: Spiral
cues.notes: Still on the ball, but the specks start travelling.

cues.name: Cathedral
cues.notes: Up and out. The look everyone looks up for -- back to unison so the four columns read as one shape.

cues.name: Peak
cues.notes: Converge and diverge. Bigger than authored, because the room is full by now.

cues.name: Build
cues.notes: Vertical curtain at double speed. Passes through the ball twice a cycle, so the specks pulse on each pass.

cues.name: Drop
cues.notes: A CUT, not a fade. The one cue on this list where fade 0 is the right answer.

cues.name: Landing
cues.notes: Long way down. Back where it started, smaller and slower. The list stops here rather than wrapping.
